glosses: to grow (to let hair or nails grow without cutting them off)
to neglect, to not clean or tidy something
to lead in, to lead to the inside of
to lower something in order to cover it
to venture, to take a distant and dangerous journey
to talk at length about something

examples.text: Kilka razy zapuszczała długie włosy, ale doszła do wniosku, że jednak lepiej jej w krótkich.

glosses: nie myć, nie czyścić, nie sprzątać

examples.text: Tak zapuścił kantorek, że nie można do niego w ogóle wejść.
Krople te należy zapuszczać do oczu trzy razy dziennie.

glosses: zasłaniać rozwijając lub opuszczając coś w dół

examples.text: Wieczorem matka zapuszczała zawsze żaluzje, zanim zapaliła światło.

glosses: To become larger, to increase in magnitude.

examples.text: [...] but the dangers to trespassers, especially children, are growing, and a vigorous educational programme is urged.

glosses: To undergo growth; to be present (somewhere)

examples.text: Apples now grow all over the world.
Leaf buds grew on the trees with the advance of spring.
A long tail began to grow from his backside.
As I grew throughout adolescence, I came to appreciate many things about human nature.

glosses: To cause or allow something to become bigger, especially to cultivate plants.

examples.text: He grows peppers and squash each summer in his garden.
Have you ever grown your hair before?
The Bush administration – which sought to grow the number of fisheries managed under a program known as “catch shares”...

And — again to overgeneralize from my experience — users may not want a second Twitter either. I was a heavy Twitter user for over a decade. I loved it until I didn’t. I made connections, grew a following, floated ideas, had fun. But it also became a second, often angry, voice inside my head. Do I want to replace it with another one?

glosses: To assume a condition or quality over time.

examples.text: The boy grew wise as he matured.
My cares grew less (and less) until they evanesced completely.
In fact she was so bus doing all the things that anyone might, who finds themselves alone in an empty house, that she did not notice at first when it began to turn dusk and the rooms to grow dim.

glosses: To become attached or fixed; to adhere.

examples.text: Our knees shall kneel till to the ground they grow.
